target_customer: Online platforms (social networks, apps) that refer at-risk young users, funded by donors and grants; end users are young people who use the service free
problem: Young people struggling with mental health online are not reached by traditional care, and platforms lack a way to route at-risk users to evidence-based help.
business_model: 501(c)(3) nonprofit funded by grants and donations, with free services and platform partnerships
product_category: Nonprofit digital mental health and peer support

founders.name: Rob Morris
education: MIT, master's and PhD in media arts and sciences
previous_startups: Earlier for-profit Koko (acquired by Airbnb in 2018 per press snippets)

founders.name: Kareem Kouddous
founders.background_notes: Per the YC company page; education not listed.

competitors.name: Crisis Text Line
competitors.what: Free 24/7 text-based crisis support, with platform partnerships such as TikTok
competitors.traction_then: 1.3 million conversations in 2021 per the organization

competitors.name: 7 Cups
competitors.what: Free chat with trained non-clinician listeners plus paid therapy

technical_complexity.rationale: Moderation, risk detection and referral integrations with large platforms; AI classification was off the shelf but safety needs are high.

defensibility.rationale: Platform integrations and published trial evidence create trust and distribution that are slow to copy, but the model rests on donor funding.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed Koko; the nonprofit added partners such as TikTok, Pinterest and Snapchat according to its site.

market_need_then: Youth mental health was a prominent public concern in 2021 and 2022 and platforms faced pressure to support at-risk users; Koko cited millions reached by the batch.

branding.domain_note: Uses kokocares.org and getsupport.org rather than a bare koko.com.

identity.logo: Animated Koko logo with a color-based visual style
identity.voice_and_tone: Supportive and plain, evidence and ethics emphasized

rebrands.why: Founders retained the name when they relaunched the service as a nonprofit, per press snippets from Fast Company and MIT Media Lab.

branding.community_and_virality: Press attention including a Fast Company profile in June 2022, a Mozilla Rise25 honor for the CEO in October 2023 and widespread coverage of the January 2023 GPT-3 experiment.

brand_strength.rationale: Short memorable name with notable press and awards, but partly overshadowed by the 2023 AI consent controversy.

pivots.from: For-profit peer support startup (sold to Airbnb in 2018)
pivots.to: Nonprofit offering free services through platform partners
pivots.why: Founders restarted it as a nonprofit in late 2020 with a broader mission, per press snippets.

outcome_analysis: Koko is an active nonprofit that reaches young people through platform partnerships and claims over 10 million people reached. It is not a venture-scale company, so conventional funding rounds are not the measure; funding comes from grants and donations. The January 2023 GPT-3 experiment drew ethics criticism, and the team removed the feature. Its main strength is distribution through partner platforms and published trial evidence.
notes: Funding: only unverified aggregator figure (VCBacked about 500K pre-seed, March 2022) and a Hopelab grant for a 2023 study, amount not stated; none recorded as a round. FY2025 revenue about 1.57M from a directory, unverified. The Fast Company and MIT Media Lab pages were not opened (403 or redirect), so Airbnb 2018 sale rests on search snippets and the YC page bio. Competitor sources are partly undated organization pages; both rivals existed before 2022. Partner platform list (TikTok, Pinterest and others) comes from the company site, with start dates unverified.
